name: Quetzalcoatl
kicker: Aztec feathered-serpent god · Linked to wind, learning, and Venus
dates: Worshipped across Mesoamerica for over 1,000 years
briefing: Quetzalcoatl was the feathered-serpent god the Aztecs credited with creating humankind by grinding up old bones and mixing them with his own blood. He was linked to the wind, learning, and the planet Venus, and he feuded endlessly with his rival, Tezcatlipoca. According to a legend written down after the Spanish conquest, the Aztec ruler Moctezuma II mistook the conquistador Hernán Cortés for this god returning home — though many historians today doubt that story is true.

qb.tip: All four Middle School/Easy High School hits are clearly about this god; nearly every one also mentions his rival Tezcatlipoca, which is the Buzzer Trap below.

sample.note: 11 real QBReader tossups for this answer line (4 Middle School/Easy High School + 7 Regular High School, power-marked)

tossups.p: This deity is sometimes called the “White” counterpart of his rival, whose name means “Smoking Mirror.” According to a legend recorded after the Spanish conquest — one that many historians now doubt — the ruler Moctezuma II mistook the conquistador Hernán Cortés [“er-NAHN kor-TEZ”] for
tossups.r: this deity returning home. For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god, the rival of Tezcatlipoca [“tez-kaht-lee-POH-kah”].

tossups.p: This deity traveled to the underworld of Mictlan [“meek-TLAHN”] to gather old bones, which he ground up and mixed with his own blood to form the people of the current, fifth age of the world. This deity’s twin brother had the head of a dog and helped guide souls to the underworld.
tossups.r: That brother was named Xolotl [“SHOH-lot-ul”]. For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent god, a rival of Tezcatlipoca in Aztec mythology.

tossups.p: This deity once ordered insects to chew holes into a conch shell so it could be used as a trumpet. This deity’s calendar name was “One Reed,” and he was said to have sailed away to the east on a raft of snakes after being tricked into breaking a sacred vow while drunk with his own sister.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god of the wind and learning, who the Aztecs supposedly thought had returned when Hernán Cortés arrived.

tossups.p: This deity is associated with the planet Venus as the morning star, while his twin brother Xolotl is linked to the evening star. This deity’s long-running rivalry with Tezcatlipoca was said to have destroyed and recreated several earlier ages of the world.
tossups.r: This deity mixed the bones of those earlier humans with his own blood to form the current fifth race of people. For 10 points, name this Aztec “feathered serpent” god.

tossups.p: In one version of this deity’s birth, he came from the virgin goddess Chimalman [“chee-mahl-MAHN”] after a vision in her dream. This deity is also remembered as a patron of maize farming, and in one tale he disguised himself as a black ant to steal corn hidden inside a mountain.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god, the rival of the “Smoking Mirror” god Tezcatlipoca.

tossups.p: This deity set himself on fire out of shame after breaking a sacred vow of purity, and he rose into the sky as the morning star. This deity is sometimes identified with the wind god Ehecatl [“eh-EH-kaht-ul”], and worms once drilled holes for him into a conch shell to make music.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Aztec “feathered serpent” deity, the chief rival of Tezcatlipoca.

tossups.p: This deity’s rival tricked him into staring at his own reflection in a mirror, one of several tricks that shamed him into exile. This deity was one of the most important Aztec gods, credited with teaching humans to farm corn and serving as the patron of priests and learning.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent god whose rival was the jaguar-associated Tezcatlipoca.

tossups.p: This deity’s name combines the Nahuatl [“NAH-waht-l”] words for a brightly colored bird and a snake. This deity exiled himself on a raft of snakes after a rival tricked him into drunkenly breaking a vow with his sister, and the Aztecs later connected his promised return with the arrival of Spanish ships.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent god, the rival of Tezcatlipoca in Aztec religion.

tossups.p: This deity journeyed into the underworld with his dog-headed twin brother to gather the bones of an earlier race of humans. After grinding those bones and mixing them with blood from his own body, this deity used the mixture to create the people of the present age.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent Aztec god, a rival of Tezcatlipoca who is linked with the planet Venus.

tossups.p: This deity was sometimes shown wearing a cone-shaped hat in his aspect as a wind god, Ehecatl. According to one legend, a red ant told this deity where to find corn hidden inside a mountain, so this deity turned himself into a black ant to sneak in and steal some.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god, the rival of Tezcatlipoca.

tossups.p: This deity’s rival, whose name means “Smoking Mirror,” once lost a foot to a crocodile monster while helping form the earth. That same rival later tricked this deity into a night of shameful drinking with his own sister, which led this deity to set himself on fire.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god who rose into the sky as the morning star, the planet Venus.

tossups.p: This deity’s return was supposedly predicted for a year called “One Reed” on the Aztec calendar, a prophecy later linked to the arrival of Spanish ships, though many historians now doubt the Aztecs truly believed this. This deity journeyed to Mictlan to retrieve bones for making humans.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent god, the rival of Tezcatlipoca in Aztec mythology.

tossups.p: This deity’s twin brother guided souls to the underworld and had the head of a dog, unlike this deity’s own form as a feathered serpent. This deity repeatedly battled his rival over who would rule as the sun during the earlier ages of the world.
tossups.r: For 10 points, identify this Aztec god associated with wind and the planet Venus, the twin of Xolotl.

tossups.p: This deity’s priests were said to favor self-sacrifice through fasting and bloodletting rather than the large-scale human sacrifice linked to some other Aztec gods. This deity was credited with giving humans the calendar and the arts, in addition to teaching them to farm corn.
tossups.r: For 10 points, name this feathered-serpent god of wind and learning, the rival of the “Smoking Mirror” god Tezcatlipoca.

tossups.p: This deity mixed his own blood with bones he gathered from Mictlan to bring the current race of humans to life. According to a legend written down after the Spanish conquest, the Aztec ruler Moctezuma II supposedly mistook the conquistador Hernán Cortés for a returning version of
tossups.r: this deity — though many historians today doubt the story is accurate. For 10 points, name this Aztec feathered-serpent god.

clues.t: Name means “feathered serpent” in the Aztec language of Nahuatl
Chief rival was Tezcatlipoca, the “Smoking Mirror” god, sometimes described as his brother
A legend written after the Spanish conquest claims Moctezuma II mistook Hernán Cortés for this god’s return — a story many historians now doubt
Credited with creating the current, fifth race of humans by mixing his own blood with bones from the underworld
Associated with the planet Venus as the morning star
His twin brother, Xolotl, had the head of a dog and guided souls to the underworld
Traveled to the underworld, Mictlan, to gather the bones used to create humankind
Exiled himself by sailing east on a raft made of snakes, promising to return someday
Tricked by his rival into breaking a sacred vow while drunk; in shame, he set himself on fire and rose as the morning star
Also worshipped as Ehecatl, a wind god, and honored as the patron of learning, writing, and the arts
Known as a patron of maize farming; in one myth he turned into a black ant to steal corn hidden inside a mountain
His promised return was tied to a year called “One Reed” on the Aztec calendar
Ordered worms or insects to drill holes into a conch shell to turn it into a musical trumpet
In one origin story, born to the virgin goddess Chimalman after a vision in her dream
Tricked by Tezcatlipoca into staring at his own reflection in a mirror, which shamed him into exile
In one myth, worked with a goddess called the Snake Woman to help bring humankind to life
Shares his name with a legendary Toltec priest-king of the city of Tula, which fed later legends about his return
Sometimes called the “White Tezcatlipoca,” a counterpart to his black-mirrored rival
His rival once lost a foot to a giant crocodile monster while helping shape the earth
Served as patron of the priesthood, the calendar, and systems of writing
His worship favored fasting and bloodletting rather than the large-scale human sacrifice linked to some other Aztec gods

trap.title: Quetzalcoatl or Tezcatlipoca?
trap.body: These two rival gods appear together in almost every real tossup, so a clue about one often sits right next to a clue about the other. Tezcatlipoca (“Smoking Mirror”) is linked to night, jaguars, and sacrifice; Quetzalcoatl is the feathered serpent linked to wind, learning, and Venus. The rival is usually the one doing the tricking — he shames Quetzalcoatl into drunkenness and self-exile, not the other way around.
trap.fix: If the clue says “feathered serpent,” “wind,” “learning,” or “Venus,” it is Quetzalcoatl. If it says “Smoking Mirror,” “jaguar,” or focuses on tricking a rival, it is Tezcatlipoca.
trap.line: Real answer line: Quetzalcoatl (prompt on “Feathered Serpent” or “Plumed Serpent”)
